payload.question_text: A team is deciding between an LLM and an SLM for an on-device museum assistant limited to exhibit facts. Which evidence supports selecting an SLM over an LLM? Select all that apply.

options.text: The team needs the greatest possible number of model variables.
options.rationale: More model variables describe LLMs. That requirement would support considering an LLM instead.
options.better_fit: Use this when broad power and generalization justify a larger language model.

feedback.intrinsic: This criterion pulls the decision toward a larger model.
feedback.instructional: LLMs use more variables; SLMs fit focused topics and local deployment.

options.text: The assistant has a focused topic area.
options.rationale: SLMs are better suited to focused topics. Exhibit facts form a narrowly bounded subject area.

options.text: The assistant must run locally on visitor devices.
options.rationale: SLMs fit smaller models deployed locally. On-device use supports that choice.

options.text: The team does not need broad generalization across unrelated tasks.
options.rationale: LLMs are valued for broad generalization. A limited need for that strength supports an SLM.

payload.explanation: Correct. The focused scope, local deployment, and limited generalization need support an SLM.

criteria.mechanic_rhythm_variation: Mechanics vary naturally without disruptive repetition.
